region: Central Africa (Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cameroon, Gabon)
description: Wenge is a very dark, coarse-textured African hardwood with fine light and dark banding, used for panelling, furniture, kitchens, flooring and veneer. It splinters easily, so edges and offcuts need careful handling.

hazards.summary: The UK HSE lists wenge as a wood whose splinters are reported to go septic.
The UK HSE lists dermatitis among reported effects of wenge. It does not say whether this is irritation or allergy.
The UK HSE lists nervous system effects such as giddiness, drowsiness and visual disturbance, plus abdominal cramps, as reported effects of wenge.
All wood dust is classified as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancers of the nose and sinuses after long-term exposure. This applies to this wood like any other.

exposure_limits.note: Applies to wood dust generally; this species has no separate ACGIH value.

related_species_note: Panga panga (Millettia stuhlmannii) is a similar-looking wood sometimes sold alongside wenge; hazards above are listed for wenge only.

notes_internal: No primary peer-reviewed health reports found on PubMed for wenge / Millettia laurentii (searched 'wenge', 'Millettia laurentii', 'Millettia AND dermatitis/asthma/toxic'). All hazards rest on HSE-WIS30. Panga panga (M. stuhlmannii) deliberately not listed as a common name; it is a different species. Region and description not cited to a Tier D source.
